The source target is $\lim_{p\to\infty}Q_p=P_*$. Its needed lower
bound has the literal quantifiers
$$
\forall\varepsilon>0\quad\exists p\in\mathbb N,
\boldsymbol\gamma,\boldsymbol\beta\in\mathbb R^p:
\quad\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\mathbb E_J
\langle\psi_{n,p,J}|C_{n,J}|\psi_{n,p,J}\rangle
\ge P_*-\varepsilon.
$$
statements.section: 8. From the scalar formula to one ordinary QAOA word

statements.markdown:
[OpenAI (2026b), Theorem 1.1][Q] proves that for
every $\varepsilon>0$ there is one finite $W$ with
$v(W)\geq P_*-\varepsilon$, whose depth and angles depend on
$\varepsilon$ but not on $n$ or $J$. The instance still determines
$C_{n,J}$.
statements.section: 5.3 A fixed QAOA circuit before the thermodynamic limit

statements.markdown:
The deduction of near-optimality is now explicit:
$$
P_*-v(W)\leq
 (P_*-I_T)+|I_T-S_{T,N}|+|S_{T,N}-v(W)|.            \tag{13}
$$
Choose $T$ so that $1-T<\varepsilon/3$, then $N$ so that the
second term is below $\varepsilon/3$, and finally use Proposition 5
with $\eta<\varepsilon/3$. These finite choices give
$v(W)>P_*-\varepsilon$ before $n$ tends to infinity.
statements.section: 5.3 A fixed QAOA circuit before the thermodynamic limit

statements.markdown: The separate circuit theorem in [OpenAI (2026b)][qaoa-manuscript] resolves the eventual-optimality conjecture for the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) in [Basso–Farhi–Marwaha–Villalonga–Zhou, §7, equation (7.2)][bfmvz]. The *Long Reasoning Record*, [§8](../long/reasoning-record.md#qaoa-construction), develops its circuit construction and the order of limits. It requires additional arguments beyond full support.

These branches
explain why the two selected formal statements are not a formal proof of
the complete circuit theorem.
